A federal judge appointed by Donald Trump has, in recent months, repeatedly
broadcast live from his office, appearing on pro-Israel and right-wing
programs to promote his book denying his genocide.

On one such broadcast, the judge, Roy Altman,
[called](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CmjwZ4gGW14) the traditional
Palestinian keffiyeh scarf a "terrorism scarf." He's
[participated](https://www.meforum.org/about/about-the-middle-east-forum) in
events with a group that purports to combat "lawful Islamism" in the U.S. All
the while, he has
[bragged](https://x.com/RoyKAltman/status/2029683528581968186?s=20) about
taking 10% of the federal judicial branch on trips to Israel, and helping
ensure that other federal judges see the situation in Israel and Gaza the way
he does.

This week, a Florida attorney filed a complaint with the U.S. Court of
Appeals, accusing Altman, a judge in the Southern District of Florida, of
violating judicial ethics codes.

### 'No Genocide'

Born in Venezuela, Altman was nominated in April 2018 by President Donald
Trump, and was eventually confirmed by the Senate the next year, by a 66-33
vote. At the time, he was the youngest federal district court judge in the
U.S.

He's ruled on a variety of high-profile cases, including
[dismissing](https://www.cbsnews.com/amp/miami/news/florida-transgender-
athlete-law-challenge-rejected/) a transgender teenager's legal challenge to
Florida's law banning transgender girls from playing on women's and girl's
sports teams - and, more recently, [halting](https://www.theguardian.com/us-
news/2026/aug/06/trump-bbc-libel-lawsuit) an order requiring Trump to hand
over financial information about his empire to the BBC, amid an ongoing libel
suit Trump filed against the outlet.

But Altman has been unusually active _outside_ of his judicial mandate -
[including](https://x.com/meforum/status/2048804451792945196) _within_ the
confines of his workday, when he might otherwise be expected to be conducting
the people's work as a taxpayer-funded official of the judicial branch.
